page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine optimized for high-density compute requirements with a constrained memory footprint. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance delivers 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 80 physical cores using two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 320.0 GB, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on remote premium storage capabilities and CPU execution.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier performance across both single-threaded and massive multithreaded workloads. The CPU achieves a multi-core score of 28,767.0 in Geekbench and 288,282.1 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Memory throughput benchmarks show uncached read speeds reaching 463.81 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 210.18 GB/sec. The presence of advanced vector extensions—including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16—yields high throughput in mathematical and machine learning tasks, logging 369.6 tokens per second on prompt processing for 7B parameter models.

Cost efficiency is focused heavily on compute-centric scaling. Because memory is capped at 2.0 GB per vCPU and local storage is omitted, the instance reduces the overhead typically tied to unused RAM or unneeded local NVMe drives. System administrators must account for remote storage latency and bandwidth when deploying I/O-intensive workloads, as all persistent storage must be mounted remotely.

The Azure D160als_v7 is suitable for highly parallel compute tasks that do not demand extensive RAM per core. Key deployment profiles include large-scale software compilation, batch processing, video encoding, static web serving fleets, and CPU-based LLM inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a high-vCPU general-purpose virtual machine designed for compute-heavy parallel workloads. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running up to 4.5 GHz, it supplies 160 dedicated vCPUs across 80 physical cores alongside 320.0 GB of memory. It features a lean 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio, excludes local disk storage in favor of premium remote storage attachments, and contains no GPUs. Benchmark metrics consistently rank in the top tier, exhibiting strong CPU throughput in stress-ng and Geekbench, as well as high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 460 GB/sec for reads. Hardware vector support including AVX-512 VNNI accelerates CPU-based inference and cryptographic operations. The instance is suitable for parallel batch jobs, extensive software compilation, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
